title: Zero-Sum Triples
statement:
Find all groups of **three numbers from `nums` that add up to 0**. Two groups are the same if they contain the same three values (the order does not matter), so `[-1, 0, 1]` and `[1, 0, -1]` count once. Each number in the list can be used at most once per group (by position).

Return the **number of different groups** (counted by their values).

examples.explanation: Only the value group {0, 0, 0}, however many zeros there are.

hints.nudge: Fix the smallest number of the group. Then the other two must add up to its negative, and the rest of the list is sorted...
hints.pattern: Sort, fix one number, then use two pointers for the other two. Skip repeated values.
hints.pseudocode:
sort(nums); count = 0
for i in 0..n-3:
  if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i-1]: continue
  lo = i+1; hi = n-1
  while lo < hi:
    s = nums[i] + nums[lo] + nums[hi]
    if s < 0: lo++ elif s > 0: hi--
    else: count++; lo++; hi--; skip equal values on both sides
hints.walkthrough: Three nested loops are O(n^3). After sorting, fix the first value nums[i]; the other two must sum to -nums[i], which is a sorted pair-sum problem: move lo right when the sum is too small and hi left when it is too big. To count each value group once, skip a position if it equals the previous value at the same level (for i, and for lo/hi after finding a match). O(n^2) overall.
